## P3 - Coupled, untested `# clab-service-defaults` marker between `SaveConfig` and `filterLauncherConfig`

**Location:** [nodes/mikrotik&#95;chr/mikrotik&#95;chr.go:178-224](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/77d24e9da2cf391be6f422e382af08feb98cc581/nodes/mikrotik_chr/mikrotik_chr.go#L178-L224)

**Problem:** The marker `# clab-service-defaults` exists as two independent string literals in [`mikrotik_chr.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/77d24e9da2cf391be6f422e382af08feb98cc581/nodes/mikrotik_chr/mikrotik_chr.go#L1-L1)&#58; inside the SSH command built in `SaveConfig` &#40;line 178&#41; and as the comparison value in `filterLauncherConfig` &#40;line 213&#41;. The `serviceDefaults` branch also hard-codes the allow-list `"/ip service"` and `"/snmp"`, which must stay in lockstep with the verbose commands appended after the `:put`. No test references the marker&#58; the new branch has zero unit-test coverage, since the existing filter tests &#40;`TestFilterLauncherConfig`, `TestFilterLauncherConfigContinuationLines`, `TestFilterLauncherConfigEscapedBackslash`&#41; all use inputs without the tail.

**Trigger:** Any future edit of one side of the coupling. Dropping the `:put` marker leaves the verbose tail fully included &#40;benign duplication&#41;, but adding a new verbose section to the SSH command, such as `/ip firewall export verbose`, without updating the allow-list silently drops that entire section from the saved file, because the branch discards every post-marker section that is not `/ip service` or `/snmp`.

**Impact:** `containerlab save` would silently produce an incomplete `config.auto.rsc`, and the documented behavior that an explicit VRF override back to `main` survives the next deployment would regress without any failing check.

**Suggested correction:** Define one shared constant, for example `serviceDefaultsMarker = "# clab-service-defaults"`, used by both the command and the filter, and add one table-driven case to the filter tests covering the marker plus a verbose `/ip service` and `/snmp` tail and a dropped non-service section.


## P4 - `exportedConfig` fixture models the removed policy-table launcher; new filter path untested

**Location:** [nodes/mikrotik&#95;chr/mikrotik&#95;chr&#95;test.go:201-241](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/77d24e9da2cf391be6f422e382af08feb98cc581/nodes/mikrotik_chr/mikrotik_chr_test.go#L201-L241)

**Problem:** The fixture is commented as a verbatim `RouterOS` 7.24.5 `/export` of a node this kind deployed, but this PR changed what the kind deploys&#58; the fixture contains `/routing table add comment=clab-mgmt fib name=mgmt` and `/routing rule` lines that the VRF launcher no longer creates, and lacks the `/ip vrf add name=mgmt interfaces=ether1 comment=clab-mgmt` object and the `/ip service` and `/snmp` sections with `vrf=mgmt` that a real export now contains. `TestFilterLauncherConfig` still passes because clab-mgmt comment matching is unchanged, but the kept-list assertion for `"/routing table"` &#40;line 266&#41; now asserts against an artifact the kind will no longer produce.

**Trigger:** Every run of the unit tests after this PR.

**Impact:** No incorrect behavior today, but the suite validates the filter against a configuration shape the launcher no longer emits, and the new post-marker filtering path, the most subtle logic in the diff, runs only against pre-PR-shaped input. This compounds the duplicated-marker finding.

**Suggested correction:** Refresh `exportedConfig` to a VRF-world export including the `/ip vrf` line with `comment=clab-mgmt`, service lines carrying `vrf=mgmt`, and a marker plus verbose tail; this simultaneously closes the coverage gap for the `serviceDefaults` branch and makes the fixture description accurate again.


## Coverage

- Source-only review; no tests were executed and no `RouterOS` instance was available, so no finding here reflects a CI run result.
- `RouterOS` API semantics are unverifiable from the snapshot&#58; the `dynamic=false` filter on `/rest/ip/service`, the round-trip of `gateway=$G4@$MGMT_TABLE` in the `mgmt_in_place` query, the `vrf` parameter on `/rest/ping`, and the `LL%ether1@$MGMT_TABLE` suffix in the `tool/fetch` address. Each fails visibly if wrong &#40;node never ready or a logged gateway warning&#41;, and the unchanged e2e suite [`tests/16-mikrotik-chr/01-chr.robot`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/77d24e9da2cf391be6f422e382af08feb98cc581/tests/16-mikrotik-chr/01-chr.robot#L1-L1) exercises all of them on `RouterOS` 7.24.5 in CI.
- Edge-case behavior change, awareness only&#58; with both management addresses empty, the new final `mgmt_in_place \|\| mgmt_fail` kills the container where the base only logged and continued. Practically unreachable since containerlab always assigns management addressing, and failing loudly is defensible, but the message would be misleading if it ever fired.
- Docs and implementation are mutually consistent&#58; service list &#40;ssh, www, www-ssl, api, api-ssl, winbox, telnet, SNMP&#41;, FTP exclusion, restart semantics, the `CHR_INTF_WAIT` + 4 x `CHR_BOOT_WAIT` + 90 s start-period formula, and the fresh-container migration warning for pre-VRF nodes. The pre-VRF restart guard message matches the documented migration path.
- No topology schema or CLI API changes are involved, so no [`clab.schema.json`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/77d24e9da2cf391be6f422e382af08feb98cc581/schemas/clab.schema.json#L1-L1) review was needed. All four changed paths were read in full along with their callers &#40;`ExportConfigOverSSH`, `WriteSavedConfig`&#41; and the unchanged e2e suite.

1: ---
2: description: Behavioral guidelines to reduce common LLM coding mistakes. Use when writing, reviewing, or refactoring code to avoid overcomplication, make surgical changes, surface assumptions, and define verifiable success criteria.
3: alwaysApply: true
4: ---
5: 
6: # Karpathy behavioral guidelines
7: 
8: Behavioral guidelines to reduce common LLM coding mistakes. Merge with project-specific instructions as needed.
9: 
10: **Tradeoff:** These guidelines bias toward caution over speed. For trivial tasks, use judgment.
11: 
12: ## 1. Think Before Coding
13: 
14: **Don't assume. Don't hide confusion. Surface tradeoffs.**
15: 
16: Before implementing:
17: 
18: - State your assumptions explicitly. If uncertain, ask.
19: - If multiple interpretations exist, present them - don't pick silently.
20: - If a simpler approach exists, say so. Push back when warranted.
21: - If something is unclear, stop. Name what's confusing. Ask.
22: 
23: ## 2. Simplicity First
24: 
25: **Minimum code that solves the problem. Nothing speculative.**
26: 
27: - No features beyond what was asked.
28: - No abstractions for single-use code.
29: - No "flexibility" or "configurability" that wasn't requested.
30: - No error handling for impossible scenarios.
31: - If you write 200 lines and it could be 50, rewrite it.
32: 
33: Ask yourself: "Would a senior engineer say this is overcomplicated?" If yes, simplify.
34: 
35: ## 3. Surgical Changes
36: 
37: **Touch only what you must. Clean up only your own mess.**
38: 
39: When editing existing code:
40: 
41: - Don't "improve" adjacent code, comments, or formatting.
42: - Don't refactor things that aren't broken.
43: - Match existing style, even if you'd do it differently.
44: - If you notice unrelated dead code, mention it - don't delete it.
45: 
46: When your changes create orphans:
47: 
48: - Remove imports/variables/functions that YOUR changes made unused.
49: - Don't remove pre-existing dead code unless asked.
50: 
51: The test: Every changed line should trace directly to the user's request.
52: 
53: ## 4. Goal-Driven Execution
54: 
55: **Define success criteria. Loop until verified.**
56: 
57: Transform tasks into verifiable goals:
58: 
59: - "Add validation" → "Write tests for invalid inputs, then make them pass"
60: - "Fix the bug" → "Write a test that reproduces it, then make it pass"
61: - "Refactor X" → "Ensure tests pass before and after"
62: 
63: For multi-step tasks, state a brief plan:
64: 
65: ```
66: 1. [Step] → verify: [check]
67: 2. [Step] → verify: [check]
68: 3. [Step] → verify: [check]
69: ```
70: 
71: Strong success criteria let you loop independently. Weak criteria ("make it work") require constant clarification.
72: 
73: ---
74: 
75: **These guidelines are working if:** fewer unnecessary changes in diffs, fewer rewrites due to overcomplication, and clarifying questions come before implementation rather than after mistakes.

1: ---
2: description: Ponytail, lazy senior dev mode. Always pick the simplest solution that works.
3: globs:
4: alwaysApply: true
5: ---
6: 
7: # Ponytail, lazy senior dev mode
8: 
9: You are a lazy senior developer. Lazy means efficient, not careless. The best code is the code never written.
10: 
11: Before writing any code, stop at the first rung that holds:
12: 
13: 1. Does this need to be built at all? (YAGNI)
14: 2. Does it already exist in this codebase? Reuse the helper, util, or pattern that's already here, don't re-write it.
15: 3. Does the standard library already do this? Use it.
16: 4. Does a native platform feature cover it? Use it.
17: 5. Does an already-installed dependency solve it? Use it.
18: 6. Can this be one line? Make it one line.
19: 7. Only then: write the minimum code that works.
20: 
21: The ladder runs after you understand the problem, not instead of it: read the task and the code it touches, trace the real flow end to end, then climb.
22: 
23: Bug fix = root cause, not symptom: a report names a symptom. Grep every caller of the function you touch and fix the shared function once — one guard there is a smaller diff than one per caller, and patching only the path the ticket names leaves a sibling caller still broken.
24: 
25: Rules:
26: 
27: - No abstractions that weren't explicitly requested.
28: - No new dependency if it can be avoided.
29: - No boilerplate nobody asked for.
30: - Deletion over addition. Boring over clever. Fewest files possible.
31: - Shortest working diff wins, but only once you understand the problem. The smallest change in the wrong place isn't lazy, it's a second bug.
32: - Question complex requests: "Do you actually need X, or does Y cover it?"
33: - Pick the edge-case-correct option when two stdlib approaches are the same size, lazy means less code, not the flimsier algorithm.
34: - Mark deliberate simplifications that cut a real corner with a known ceiling (global lock, O(n²) scan, naive heuristic) with a `ponytail:` comment naming the ceiling and upgrade path.
35: 
36: Not lazy about: understanding the problem (read it fully and trace the real flow before picking a rung, a small diff you don't understand is just laziness dressed up as efficiency), input validation at trust boundaries, error handling that prevents data loss, security, accessibility, the calibration real hardware needs (the platform is never the spec ideal, a clock drifts, a sensor reads off), anything explicitly requested. Lazy code without its check is unfinished: non-trivial logic leaves ONE runnable check behind, the smallest thing that fails if the logic breaks (an assert-based demo/self-check or one small test file; no frameworks, no fixtures). Trivial one-liners need no test.

(End of file - total 36 lines)
</content>

25: +[`containerlab save`](../../cmd/save.md) writes each node's `/export` to `ftpboot/config.auto.rsc` in its lab directory. Service settings include their defaults so an explicit VRF override back to `main` survives the next deployment.

27:  ### Node readiness
28:  
29:  The node is ready once RouterOS accepted the credentials and the startup config, reaches its gateway from the management address and, unless the configuration disables SSH, its SSH server answers. An SSH server that does not answer within `CHR_BOOT_WAIT` is logged, and the node is still declared ready, since REST and the console work. The container log then shows

59:  ## Management connectivity
60:  
61: -Management is transparent: the IPv4 and IPv6 addresses and gateways containerlab gives the node's `eth0` are configured on RouterOS `ether1`, and the container's `eth0` is bridged to the VM's `ether1`. The router is the node's management address: SSH, the REST API, Winbox, SNMP and every other service answer on it, LLDP/MNDP work on the management network, and the address in the topology table is the one in the RouterOS configuration.
62: +Management is transparent: the IPv4 and IPv6 addresses and gateways containerlab gives the node's `eth0` are configured on RouterOS `ether1`, and the container's `eth0` is bridged to the VM's `ether1`. The address in the topology table is the one in the RouterOS configuration.
63:  
64:  The image ships busybox only (no `tc`), so where vrnetlab's [transparent management](../vrnetlab.md#management-interface) redirects with tc-mirred, this kind uses a Linux bridge. The container itself has no address on the management network; it reaches RouterOS for bootstrap over IPv6 link-local on that bridge.
65:  
66: -The management return path lives in its own routing table, `mgmt`, selected by routing rules for the management addresses, and CHR's `ether1` DHCP client is disabled. A default route in the lab configuration, a PPPoE client's default route or a dual-WAN setup in `main` therefore does not cut SSH or REST access to the node. RouterOS's router advertisements on `ether1` carry a zero router lifetime, so no host on the management network takes the router as its IPv6 default gateway; the container joins the management network only once this is in place. The objects carry the comment `clab-mgmt` and are re-applied at boot when the container's addressing changed.
67: +The launcher places `ether1` in a native `mgmt` VRF before `main`. RouterOS creates its routing table and connected routes; the launcher adds IPv4 and IPv6 defaults that resolve their gateways in `mgmt`. No source-policy rules or route leaks are added. Data interfaces remain in `main`, so a lab default route does not take management replies away from `ether1`. CHR's `ether1` DHCP client is disabled.
68: +
69: +On first boot, one RouterOS background job creates the VRF and binds SSH, HTTP/HTTPS (including REST), API/API-SSL, Winbox, Telnet and SNMP to it. Their enabled/disabled state is preserved. The launcher waits for the native routing table and service bindings before configuring management addressing, joining the external management bridge and fetching the startup config through `mgmt`. On restart, startup-config service overrides are preserved. The launcher uses HTTP/REST with the topology credentials during container startup. SSH in `mgmt` provides user login access and is also used by `containerlab save`. Credential setup, service ports and access controls are unchanged.
70: +
71: +A service's VRF binding also changes where it can be reached: these services no longer listen through data interfaces in `main` unless the startup config changes their binding. RouterOS FTP does not support VRF binding and is unavailable through the management VRF. Other router-originated services, such as DNS, NTP and logging, need their own VRF-aware configuration to use management egress. RouterOS applies its VRF interface matching to firewall rules; see the [RouterOS VRF documentation](https://manual.mikrotik.com/docs/user-guides/routing-and-networking-protocols/vrf/).
72: +
73: +VRF membership does not disable Layer 2 neighbor discovery. LLDP, CDP and MNDP follow `/ip neighbor discovery-settings`; use an explicit interface list excluding `ether1` when management discovery is unwanted.
74: +
75: +RouterOS's router advertisements on `ether1` carry a zero router lifetime, so no host on the management network takes the router as its IPv6 default gateway. The container joins the management network only once this is in place. Management objects carry the comment `clab-mgmt` and are re-applied at boot when the container's addressing changed.
76:  
77:  /// warning
78: -Do not remove or change the `clab-mgmt` objects or the `mgmt` routing table: management of the node depends on them.
79: +Do not remove or change the `clab-mgmt` objects or the `mgmt` VRF: management of the node depends on them. This setup requires a fresh node container; it does not migrate a running node that uses the previous policy-only `mgmt` table. Export the user configuration before recreating such a node.
80:  ///
81:  
82:  ## Restarts
83:  
84:  [`containerlab restart`](../../cmd/restart.md) and a `/system reboot` inside RouterOS keep the interface names, MAC addresses, configuration and links: the launcher persists the NIC identity in the container on first boot and does not re-run the bootstrap. A plain `docker restart` keeps the router and its management, but Docker deletes the node's veth links, which stay down until the node is restarted with containerlab or the lab is redeployed.

The objects carry the comment `clab-mgmt` and are re-applied at boot when the container's addressing changed.\n67: +The launcher places `ether1` in a native `mgmt` VRF before `main`. RouterOS creates its routing table and connected routes; the launcher adds IPv4 and IPv6 defaults that resolve their gateways in `mgmt`. No source-policy rules or route leaks are added. Data interfaces remain in `main`, so a lab default route does not take management replies away from `ether1`. CHR's `ether1` DHCP client is disabled.\n68: +\n69: +On first boot, one RouterOS background job creates the VRF and binds SSH, HTTP/HTTPS (including REST), API/API-SSL, Winbox, Telnet and SNMP to it. The launcher waits for the native routing table and service bindings before configuring management addressing, joining the external management bridge and fetching the startup config through `mgmt`. On restart, startup-config service overrides are preserved. The launcher uses HTTP/REST with the topology credentials during container startup. SSH in `mgmt` provides user login access and is also used by `containerlab save`. Credential setup, service ports and access controls are unchanged.\n70: +\n71: +A service's VRF binding also changes where it can be reached: these services no longer listen through data interfaces in `main` unless the startup config changes their binding. RouterOS FTP does not support VRF binding and is unavailable through the management VRF. Other router-originated services, such as DNS, NTP and logging, need their own VRF-aware configuration to use management egress. RouterOS applies its VRF interface matching to firewall rules; see the [RouterOS VRF documentation](https://manual.mikrotik.com/docs/user-guides/routing-and-networking-protocols/vrf/).\n72: +\n73: +VRF membership does not disable Layer 2 neighbor discovery. <type>file</type>
<content>
1: #!/bin/sh
2: # chr-launch.sh: run the OFFICIAL mikrotik/chr image (MikroTik RouterOS Cloud
3: # Hosted Router) as a containerlab node, image untouched.
4: #
5: # The image is MikroTik's own Docker Hub distribution (Alpine + qemu +
6: # /diskimage/chr-<ver>.img + /start.sh). This script is bind-mounted into the
7: # node and set as its entrypoint by the containerlab `mikrotik_chr` kind. It replaces
8: # the image's /start.sh, which is not orchestration-ready (containerlab#3116):
9: # it scans interfaces once before containerlab attaches the links, bridges the
10: # management NIC so the container IP never reaches the router, and imports no
11: # startup config.
12: #
13: # What it does (vrnetlab's mikrotik/routeros launch.py is the model, re-done
14: # with the image's own busybox + qemu: no python, no ftp client, no tc):
15: #   1. waits for the CLAB_INTFS data interfaces containerlab attaches (eth1..N)
16: #   2. management, transparent: the container's eth0 is bridged with the VM's
17: #      ether1 tap, and eth0's addresses and default gateways move into RouterOS
18: #      ether1. The router IS the node's management address: every service and
19: #      LLDP reach it directly, nothing is port-forwarded. The image ships only
20: #      busybox (no tc), so this uses a bridge where vrnetlab uses tc-mirred
21: #   3. data: one tap per container interface, bridged pairwise (ethN <-> tapN,
22: #      LLDP forwarded). NIC order in the VM follows the eth index, so container
23: #      ethN is always RouterOS ether(N+1), even with gaps
24: #   4. after boot, over IPv6 link-local on the management bridge (no address is
25: #      added to the management network): sets the credentials and the identity,
26: #      configures ether1 with the management addresses and keeps their return
27: #      path in its own VRF (`mgmt`, below), then fetches
28: #      /ftpboot/config.auto.rsc (the containerlab startup-config, when present)
29: #      from the launcher and `/import`s it
30: #   5. prints the ready marker on the container log and waits on qemu
31: #
32: # Restart (docker restart, containerlab restart --node): RouterOS keys an
33: # ethernet interface on its MAC. A NIC that comes back with a new MAC is a NEW
34: # device (ether1 becomes ether3) and the DHCP client bound to ether1 never
35: # binds. Docker re-rolls the container's eth0 MAC whenever the netns is
36: # recreated, so the node id that seeds every NIC MAC and the data NIC count are
37: # persisted in the container on the first boot and reused: the restarted qemu
38: # carries the same NICs in the same order and RouterOS keeps ether1..N and
39: # their config. The REST bootstrap is skipped on a restart; the management
40: # step re-runs and re-applies the container's current addressing.
41: #
42: # Architectures: the image's own qemu (qemu-system-x86_64 on amd64,
43: #   qemu-system-aarch64 + edk2 on arm64), KVM when /dev/kvm exists, else TCG.
44: # Args (the kind's Cmd): --hostname H [--username U --password P]
45: #   (unknown flags are ignored); credentials default to the USERNAME/PASSWORD env
46: # Env (all optional, set under the node's `env:`); MEM, CPUS and DISK are the
47: #   official image's own variables:
48: #   MEM (qemu -m value, default 256 MiB + 8 MiB per data NIC and vCPU), CPUS (default 1),
49: #   DISK (default 128M), CHR_INTF_WAIT (s, 60), CHR_BOOT_WAIT (s, 300)
50: # Serial console: port 5000 inside the container
51: #   (docker exec -it <node> nc 127.0.0.1 5000); the container itself has no
52: #   address on the management network.
53: # Ready: /.chr-launch-ready exists once RouterOS is ready (the kind's default
54: #   healthcheck); it is removed at every start.
55: # Log lines (docker logs clab-<lab>-<node>), all prefixed "chr-launch:":
56: #   "RouterOS ready"                   login + startup config done
57: #   "startup config import FAILED: …"  the router rejected the .rsc (RouterOS's
58: #                                      own reason, with the line number)
59: #   "credential bootstrap FAILED: …"   the user/password step failed
60: #   "management setup FAILED: …"       the ether1 address / mgmt VRF step failed
61: #
62: # Copyright 2026 NetPilot Labs
63: # Licensed under the BSD 3-Clause License.
64: # SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause
65: 
66: set -u
67: 
68: # Credentials come from the USERNAME/PASSWORD env the kind sets (no quoting
69: # limits on the password); --username/--password still override them.
70: USERNAME="${USERNAME:-admin}"
71: PASSWORD="${PASSWORD-admin}"
72: HOSTNAME_ARG=""
73: while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
74:     case "$1" in
75:         --username) USERNAME="$2"; shift 2 ;;
76:         --password) PASSWORD="$2"; shift 2 ;;
77:         --hostname) HOSTNAME_ARG="$2"; shift 2 ;;
78:         --connection-mode) shift 2 ;;
79:         --trace) shift ;;
80:         *) shift ;;
81:     esac
82: done
83: [ -n "$HOSTNAME_ARG" ] || HOSTNAME_ARG="$(hostname)"
84: 
85: CPUS="${CPUS:-1}"
86: DISK="${DISK:-128M}"
87: INTF_WAIT="${CHR_INTF_WAIT:-60}"
88: BOOT_WAIT="${CHR_BOOT_WAIT:-300}"
89: INTFS="${CLAB_INTFS:-0}"
90: STARTUP_CFG=/ftpboot/config.auto.rsc
91: # Per-container state in the rw layer: survives every restart, gone with the
92: # container (destroy, redeploy --cleanup).
93: DONE_MARKER=/.chr-launch-bootstrapped
94: READY_FILE=/.chr-launch-ready
95: ID_FILE=/.chr-launch-node-id
96: NICS_FILE=/.chr-launch-nics
97: MGMT_TABLE=mgmt
98: # every management object the launcher creates carries this comment, so each
99: # boot can find and re-apply them, and SaveConfig can leave them out
100: MGMT_COMMENT=clab-mgmt
101: MGMT_BR=br0
102: # eth0's addressing as last seen: a launcher re-run in the same network
103: # namespace finds eth0 already bridged and bare
104: MGMT_FILE=/.chr-launch-mgmt
105: SYSNET=/sys/class/net
106: 
107: log() { echo "chr-launch: $*"; }
108: rm -f "$READY_FILE"
109: 
110: FETCH_PORT=8080
111: 
112: # ---- disk -----------------------------------------------------------------
113: IMG=""
114: for f in /diskimage/*.img; do [ -f "$f" ] && IMG="$f" && break; done
115: if [ -z "$IMG" ]; then
116:     log "no /diskimage/*.img in this image: not a RouterOS CHR image"
117:     exit 1
118: fi
119: # Only GROW the disk to the floor: an image already larger keeps its tail.
120: disk_bytes() {
121:     case "$1" in
122:         *G|*g) echo $(( ${1%[Gg]} * 1024 * 1024 * 1024 )) ;;
123:         *M|*m) echo $(( ${1%[Mm]} * 1024 * 1024 )) ;;
124:         *K|*k) echo $(( ${1%[Kk]} * 1024 )) ;;
125:         *) echo "$1" ;;
126:     esac
127: }
128: want_bytes="$(disk_bytes "$DISK")"
129: cur_bytes="$(stat -c %s "$IMG" 2>/dev/null || wc -c < "$IMG")"
130: if [ "$cur_bytes" -lt "$want_bytes" ] 2>/dev/null; then
131:     truncate -s "$DISK" "$IMG"
132: fi
133: 
134: # ---- wait for containerlab's data interfaces ------------------------------
135: # shellcheck disable=SC2012  # interface names are ethN, ls is safe here
136: count_intfs() { ls -d "$SYSNET"/eth[1-9]* 2>/dev/null | wc -l; }
137: waited=0
138: while [ "$(count_intfs)" -lt "$INTFS" ] && [ "$waited" -lt "$INTF_WAIT" ]; do
139:     sleep 1
140:     waited=$((waited + 1))
141: done
142: log "interfaces: $(count_intfs) of $INTFS expected after ${waited}s"
143: 
144: # ---- qemu command line ----------------------------------------------------
145: # The image's own qemu and firmware, as its /start.sh selects them.
146: case "$(uname -m)" in
147:     aarch64|arm64)
148:         QEMU="qemu-system-aarch64 -M virt -pflash /usr/share/qemu/edk2-aarch64-code.fd"
149:         TCG_CPU="-cpu cortex-a57" ;;
150:     *)
151:         QEMU="qemu-system-x86_64"
152:         TCG_CPU="" ;;
153: esac
154: if [ -e /dev/kvm ]; then
155:     ACCEL="-cpu host -accel kvm"
156: else
157:     ACCEL="$TCG_CPU -accel tcg,split-wx=on"
158:     log "no /dev/kvm: running under TCG emulation (slow boot)"
159: fi
160: 
161: # MACs: unique per node AND per NIC. The container's eth0 MAC is unique per
162: # node, so its LAST TWO octets identify the node; the NIC's last byte is the
163: # interface index (00 = mgmt, 01 = ether2, …). Two nodes sharing a NIC MAC on
164: # a link drop each other's frames as their own. The id is read on the FIRST
165: # boot only and persisted (see Restart in the header).
166: node_id="$(cat "$ID_FILE" 2>/dev/null)"
167: case "$node_id" in
168:     [0-9a-f][0-9a-f]:[0-9a-f][0-9a-f]) ;;
169:     *)
170:         e="$(cat "$SYSNET/eth0/address" 2>/dev/null)"
171:         if [ -n "$e" ]; then
172:             o2="${e##*:}"; rest_mac="${e%:*}"; o1="${rest_mac##*:}"
173:             node_id="$o1:$o2"
174:         else
175:             node_id="$(hexdump -n2 -e '2/1 "%02x:"' /dev/urandom | sed 's/:$//')"
176:         fi
177:         printf '%s\n' "$node_id" > "$ID_FILE" 2>/dev/null \
178:             || log "node id $node_id not persisted: a restart will renumber the NICs"
179:         ;;
180: esac
181: NET="-netdev tap,id=mgmt,ifname=tap0,script=no,downscript=no -device virtio-net,netdev=mgmt,mac=52:54:00:$node_id:00"
182: 
183: # ---- management: eth0 + tap0 on one bridge, eth0's addressing to the VM ----
184: ip_global() { # ip_global <4|6> <dev>: the first global address/prefix
185:     ip -"$1" addr show dev "$2" 2>/dev/null \
186:         | sed -n '/scope global/s/^ *inet6\{0,1\} \([^ ]*\) .*/\1/p' | head -n1
187: }
188: ip_gw() { # ip_gw <4|6>: the default gateway
189:     ip -"$1" route show default 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^default via \([^ ]*\) .*/\1/p' | head -n1
190: }
191: M4="$(ip_global 4 eth0)"; M6="$(ip_global 6 eth0)"
192: G4="$(ip_gw 4)"; G6="$(ip_gw 6)"
193: if [ -n "$M4$M6" ]; then
194:     printf 'M4=%s\nM6=%s\nG4=%s\nG6=%s\n' "$M4" "$M6" "$G4" "$G6" > "$MGMT_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true
195: elif [ -f "$MGMT_FILE" ]; then
196:     # shellcheck disable=SC1090  # written by this script, four plain assignments
197:     . "$MGMT_FILE"
198: fi
199: log "management: ${M4:-no IPv4}${M6:+, $M6} via ${G4:-no gateway}${G6:+, $G6}"
200: 
201: tunctl -t tap0 >/dev/null 2>&1 || ip tuntap add dev tap0 mode tap
202: if [ ! -e "$SYSNET/$MGMT_BR" ]; then
203:     _mtu="$(cat "$SYSNET/eth0/mtu" 2>/dev/null || echo 1500)"
204:     ip addr flush dev eth0
205:     # The launcher's side of the bootstrap channel: IPv6 link-local on the
206:     # bridge only. eth0 and tap0 are plain bridge ports.
207:     sysctl -qw net.ipv6.conf.default.disable_ipv6=0 net.ipv6.conf.default.accept_ra=0 2>/dev/null
208:     brctl addbr "$MGMT_BR"
209:     brctl setfd "$MGMT_BR" 0 2>/dev/null
210:     echo 16384 > "$SYSNET/$MGMT_BR/bridge/group_fwd_mask" 2>/dev/null
211:     ip link set "$MGMT_BR" address "52:54:01:$node_id:00"
212:     ip link set tap0 mtu "$_mtu"
213:     ip link set "$MGMT_BR" mtu "$_mtu"
214:     # eth0 joins the bridge only once ether1 is configured (mgmt_attach): until
215:     # then nothing the router sends (its boot-time router advertisements, CHR's
216:     # DHCP discovers) reaches the management network.
217:     brctl addif "$MGMT_BR" tap0
218:     sysctl -qw net.ipv6.conf.eth0.disable_ipv6=1 net.ipv6.conf.tap0.disable_ipv6=1 \
219:         "net.ipv6.conf.$MGMT_BR.disable_ipv6=0" "net.ipv6.conf.$MGMT_BR.accept_ra=0" \
220:         "net.ipv6.conf.$MGMT_BR.router_solicitations=0" 2>/dev/null
221: fi
222: ip link set tap0 up
223: ip link set "$MGMT_BR" up
224: # RouterOS's ether1 link-local address, from the MAC this script gives it
225: VM_LL="fe80::5054:ff:fe${node_id%%:*}:${node_id##*:}00"
226: VM_EP="$VM_LL%$MGMT_BR"
227: # The bridge's own link-local address (the startup-config fetch source). Read
228: # once qemu runs: until then tap0, the bridge's only port, has no carrier and
229: # the address stays tentative.
230: LL=""
231: bridge_ll() {
232:     _w=0
233:     while [ -z "$LL" ] && [ "$_w" -lt 20 ]; do
234:         LL="$(ip -6 addr show dev "$MGMT_BR" 2>/dev/null | grep -v tentative \
235:             | sed -n 's/^ *inet6 \(fe80::[^/]*\)\/64 .*/\1/p' | head -n1)"
236:         [ -n "$LL" ] || { sleep 1; _w=$((_w + 1)); }
237:     done
238:     [ -n "$LL" ] || log "no IPv6 link-local on $MGMT_BR"
239: }
240: 
241: # NIC order = PCI order = the order of the -device args below. Walk
242: # eth1..ethMAX so a gap (links on ether2 and ether5 only) keeps RouterOS
243: # numbering aligned: a missing ethN still gets a tap, just no bridge. The count
244: # never shrinks across restarts: a `docker restart` recreates the netns and
245: # every lab veth of the node is gone, and a NIC absent for one boot loses the
246: # config bound to it. The tap keeps ether(N+1) a real interface, its link comes
247: # back when containerlab restores the veth or the lab is redeployed.
248: max=0
249: for d in "$SYSNET"/eth[1-9]*; do
250:     [ -e "$d" ] || continue
251:     n="${d##*/eth}"
252:     [ "$n" -gt "$max" ] && max="$n"
253: done
254: prev="$(cat "$NICS_FILE" 2>/dev/null)"
255: case "$prev" in *[!0-9]*|"") prev=0 ;; esac
256: [ "$prev" -gt "$max" ] && max="$prev"
257: # The wait above can end short of CLAB_INTFS on a large lab (links attach after
258: # every container started): the NIC set still spans the expected count, and
259: # the watcher bridges the late veths.
260: case "$INTFS" in *[!0-9]*|"") INTFS=0 ;; esac
261: [ "$INTFS" -gt "$max" ] && max="$INTFS"
262: [ "$max" -gt "$prev" ] && { printf '%s\n' "$max" > "$NICS_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true; }
263: 
264: # RouterOS v7 memory ≈ 256 + 8·CPUS·(ifaces) MiB (MikroTik CHR system
265: # requirements). Scale by the HIGHEST generated NIC, not CLAB_INTFS: a sparse
266: # link on ether64 means CLAB_INTFS=1 yet 63 data NICs are created below.
267: if [ -z "${MEM:-}" ]; then
268:     MEM=$((256 + 8 * CPUS * max))
269: fi
270: 
271: bridge_eth() { # bridge_eth <i>: container ethI joins brI beside tapI (brI made once)
272:     _mtu="$(cat "$SYSNET/eth$1/mtu" 2>/dev/null || echo 1500)"
273:     if [ ! -e "$SYSNET/br$1" ]; then
274:         brctl addbr "br$1"
275:         ip link set "br$1" mtu "$_mtu"
276:         ip link set "tap$1" mtu "$_mtu"
277:         # forward LLDP (01:80:c2:00:00:0e, bit 14); STP/LACP cannot cross a bridge
278:         echo 16384 > "$SYSNET/br$1/bridge/group_fwd_mask" 2>/dev/null
279:         brctl addif "br$1" "tap$1"
280:     fi
281:     brctl addif "br$1" "eth$1"
282:     ip link set "eth$1" up
283:     ip link set "br$1" up
284: }
285: # A veth that lands or returns while qemu runs (containerlab restores a link
286: # right after a restart --node, a large lab attaches late, a peer node's
287: # redeploy recreates the pair) joins its bridge as it appears, so the RouterOS
288: # interface behind tapN gets its link back without a restart here.
289: watch_links() {
290:     _warned=""
291:     while kill -0 "$QEMU_PID" 2>/dev/null; do
292:         i=1
293:         while [ "$i" -le "$max" ]; do
294:             if [ -e "$SYSNET/eth$i" ] && [ ! -e "$SYSNET/br$i/brif/eth$i" ]; then
295:                 bridge_eth "$i" && log "link eth$i attached: bridged to tap$i"
296:             fi
297:             i=$((i + 1))
298:         done
299:         for d in "$SYSNET"/eth[1-9]*; do
300:             [ -e "$d" ] || continue
301:             n="${d##*/eth}"
302:             [ "$n" -gt "$max" ] || continue
303:             case " $_warned " in *" $n "*) continue ;; esac
304:             _warned="$_warned $n"
305:             log "link eth$n attached after qemu started with $max data NICs: no RouterOS interface for it until the node is restarted"
306:         done
307:         sleep 2
308:     done
309: }
310: 
311: i=1
312: while [ "$i" -le "$max" ]; do
313:     tap="tap$i"
314:     tunctl -t "$tap" >/dev/null 2>&1 || ip tuntap add dev "$tap" mode tap
315:     [ -e "$SYSNET/eth$i" ] && bridge_eth "$i"
316:     ip link set "$tap" up
317:     mac="$(printf '52:54:00:%s:%02x' "$node_id" "$((i & 255))")"
318:     NET="$NET -netdev tap,id=d$i,ifname=$tap,script=no,downscript=no -device virtio-net,netdev=d$i,mac=$mac"
319:     i=$((i + 1))
320: done
321: 
322: # shellcheck disable=SC2086
323: $QEMU $ACCEL -display none -monitor none \
324:     -m "$MEM" -smp "cpus=$CPUS" \
325:     -drive "file=$IMG,format=raw" \
326:     -serial telnet:0.0.0.0:5000,server,nowait \
327:     $NET &
328: QEMU_PID=$!
329: trap 'kill "$QEMU_PID" 2>/dev/null; wait "$QEMU_PID" 2>/dev/null; exit 0' TERM INT
330: log "qemu started (pid $QEMU_PID, mem ${MEM}M, cpus $CPUS, data nics $max)"
331: watch_links &
332: 
333: # ---- REST helpers ---------------------------------------------------------
334: json_str() { printf '%s' "$1" | sed 's/\\/\\\\/g; s/"/\\"/g'; }
335: rest() { # rest <user:pass> <path> [json]
336:     # Basic auth in a header, never in the URL: a password containing a URI
337:     # delimiter (#, ?, /) would change where the authority ends. REST_T is the
338:     # read timeout (default 20s).
339:     _auth="Authorization: Basic $(printf '%s' "$1" | base64 | tr -d '\n')"
340:     if [ $# -ge 3 ]; then
341:         wget -q -O- -T "${REST_T:-20}" --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
342:             --header "$_auth" --post-data "$3" "http://[$VM_EP]/rest/$2" 2>/dev/null
343:     else
344:         wget -q -O- -T "${REST_T:-20}" --header "$_auth" "http://[$VM_EP]/rest/$2" 2>/dev/null
345:     fi
346: }
347: # busybox wget discards the body of an HTTP error response, and RouterOS puts
348: # its diagnosis ONLY there ({"detail":"Script Error: … (line N column M)"}; its
349: # /log stays silent). So the calls whose failure must be readable go over a raw
350: # HTTP POST through busybox nc. busybox nc exits the moment stdin hits EOF,
351: # reply or not, and RouterOS keeps the connection open despite
352: # `Connection: close`, so the request side is held open on a fifo and closed
353: # once Content-Length bytes of body have arrived.
354: resp_complete() { # resp_complete <file>: headers + Content-Length bytes of body arrived
355:     _cl="$(grep -i -m1 '^Content-Length:' "$1" 2>/dev/null | tr -dc '0-9')"
356:     [ -n "$_cl" ] || return 1
357:     grep -q -m1 '^\r*$' "$1" 2>/dev/null || return 1
358:     [ "$(sed '1,/^\r*$/d' "$1" | wc -c | tr -d ' ')" -ge "$_cl" ]
359: }
360: rest_raw() { # rest_raw <user:pass> <path> <json> <timeout-s>  -> "<status> <body>"
361:     _f="/tmp/chr-rest.$$"; rm -f "$_f" "$_f.out"; mkfifo "$_f" || return 1
362:     timeout "$(( $4 + 5 ))" nc "$VM_EP" 80 <"$_f" >"$_f.out" 2>/dev/null &
363:     _pid=$!
364:     exec 7>"$_f"
365:     printf 'POST /rest/%s HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: [%s]\r\nAuthorization: Basic %s\r\nContent-Type: application/json\r\nContent-Length: %s\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n%s' \
366:         "$2" "$VM_LL" "$(printf '%s' "$1" | base64 | tr -d '\n')" \
367:         "$(printf '%s' "$3" | wc -c | tr -d ' ')" "$3" >&7
368:     _left=$4
369:     while kill -0 "$_pid" 2>/dev/null && ! resp_complete "$_f.out" && [ "$_left" -gt 0 ]; do
370:         sleep 1; _left=$(( _left - 1 ))
371:     done
372:     exec 7>&-
373:     wait "$_pid" 2>/dev/null
374:     _st="$(head -n1 "$_f.out" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\r' | cut -d' ' -f2)"
375:     _body="$(sed '1,/^\r*$/d' "$_f.out" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\r')"
376:     rm -f "$_f" "$_f.out"
377:     printf '%s %s' "${_st:-000}" "$_body"
378: }
379: # RouterOS REST returns the object/array on success and an empty body for a
380: # bare `set`: only an explicit error object is a failure here. A silently
381: # failed call is caught by the read-back checks that follow each step.
382: is_err() { case "$1" in *'"error"'*) return 0 ;; *) return 1 ;; esac; }
383: 
384: # ---- wait for RouterOS ----------------------------------------------------
385: waited=0
386: AUTH=""
387: # A fresh official CHR disk has ONLY the factory `admin` account (blank
388: # password): the first boot authenticates as that account whatever --username
389: # asks for, and the requested user is created below. On a restart the pair that
390: # answers is the requested user.
391: while [ -z "$AUTH" ]; do
392:     for _cred in "admin:" "admin:$PASSWORD" "$USERNAME:$PASSWORD"; do
393:         rest "$_cred" system/resource >/dev/null 2>&1 && { AUTH="$_cred"; break; }
394:     done
395:     [ -n "$AUTH" ] && break
396:     if ! kill -0 "$QEMU_PID" 2>/dev/null; then
397:         log "qemu exited during boot"
398:         exit 1
399:     fi
400:     sleep 2
401:     waited=$((waited + 2))
402:     if [ "$waited" -ge "$BOOT_WAIT" ]; then
403:         log "RouterOS did not answer within ${BOOT_WAIT}s: leaving qemu running"
404:         wait "$QEMU_PID"
405:         exit 1
406:     fi
407: done
408: log "RouterOS answered after ${waited}s"
409: 
410: # Ready means a user can log in: RouterOS starts its SSH server well after REST
411: # answers on a slow boot (about 40 s later under TCG on arm64), so when the
412: # configuration keeps SSH enabled, its port must send the banner first.
413: # A config that disables SSH is not waited for; a banner that never comes is
414: # logged and the node is still declared ready (REST works).
415: ssh_banner() { (sleep 3) | nc "$VM_EP" 22 2>/dev/null | head -c 7; }
416: ready() {
417:     case "$(rest "$AUTH" "ip/service?name=ssh")" in
418:         *'"disabled":"false"'*)
419:             _t0=$(date +%s)
420:             until [ "$(ssh_banner)" = "SSH-2.0" ]; do
421:                 if [ $(( $(date +%s) - _t0 )) -ge "$BOOT_WAIT" ]; then
422:                     log "SSH did not answer within $(( $(date +%s) - _t0 ))s (REST works)"
423:                     break
424:                 fi
425:                 sleep 2
426:             done
427:             ;;
428:     esac
429:     touch "$READY_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true
430:     log "RouterOS ready"
431: }
432: 
433: # A failed step WITHHOLDS the ready marker (qemu keeps running, so the node can
434: # still be inspected over the serial console, port 5000 in the container).
435: bootstrap_fail() {
436:     log "credential bootstrap FAILED: $1"
437:     wait "$QEMU_PID"
438:     exit 0
439: }
440: 
441: # ---- management: ether1 in its own VRF -------------------------------------
442: # The VRF owns its routing table and connected routes. Services must bind to
443: # it explicitly; source-policy rules are unnecessary. The link-local REST
444: # channel survives the handoff once www and ether1 belong to the same VRF.
445: mgmt_fail() {
446:     log "management setup FAILED: $1 (redeploy the node: containerlab deploy --reconfigure)"
447:     wait "$QEMU_PID"
448:     exit 0
449: }
450: rest_has() { # rest_has <path?query>: the GET answered a non-empty JSON array
451:     case "$(rest "$AUTH" "$1")" in '['*'{'*) return 0 ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
452: }
453: rest_add() { # rest_add <what> <path> <json>: a 2xx with no error object, else mgmt_fail with the router's detail
454:     _r="$(rest_raw "$AUTH" "$2" "$3" 20)"
455:     case "$_r" in
456:         2??\ *) is_err "$_r" && mgmt_fail "$1: ${_r#* }" ;;
457:         *) mgmt_fail "$1: ${_r:-no response}" ;;
458:     esac
459: }
460: rest_count() { # rest_count <path?query>: number of objects the GET answered
461:     rest "$AUTH" "$1" | tr '{' '\n' | grep -c '"\.id"'
462: }
463: rest_clear() { # rest_clear <menu>: remove its clab-mgmt objects
464:     _ids="$(rest "$AUTH" "$1?comment=$MGMT_COMMENT" | tr '{' '\n' \
465:         | sed -n 's/.*"\.id":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | paste -sd, -)"
466:     [ -z "$_ids" ] || rest_add "remove old $1" "$1/remove" "{\".id\":\"$_ids\"}"
467: }
468: # A native VRF creates its routing table asynchronously. Move the interface
469: # and services together in a router-local background job, then prove the
470: # handoff before configuring addresses/routes or attaching external eth0.
471: mgmt_vrf_ready() {
472:     rest_has "ip/vrf?name=$MGMT_TABLE&interfaces=ether1&comment=$MGMT_COMMENT&disabled=false" || return 1
473:     rest_has "routing/table?name=$MGMT_TABLE&dynamic=true&invalid=false" || return 1
474:     for _svc in ssh www www-ssl api api-ssl winbox telnet; do
475:         rest_has "ip/service?name=$_svc&vrf=$MGMT_TABLE&dynamic=false" || return 1
476:     done
477:     case "$(rest "$AUTH" snmp)" in
478:         *"\"vrf\":\"$MGMT_TABLE\""*) return 0 ;;
479:         *) return 1 ;;
480:     esac
481: }
482: mgmt_vrf() {
483:     if rest_has "ip/vrf?name=$MGMT_TABLE&interfaces=ether1&comment=$MGMT_COMMENT&disabled=false"; then
484:         # User service overrides are applied by startup-config, after the
485:         # first-boot defaults. Do not overwrite them on a restart.
486:         [ -f "$DONE_MARKER" ] && return 0
487:     else
488:         if rest_has "routing/table?name=$MGMT_TABLE"; then
489:             mgmt_fail "table $MGMT_TABLE already exists without the launcher's VRF; use a fresh container"
490:         fi
491:         _script=":delay 1s; /ip vrf add name=$MGMT_TABLE interfaces=ether1 place-before=0 comment=$MGMT_COMMENT; /ip service set ssh,www,www-ssl,api,api-ssl,winbox,telnet vrf=$MGMT_TABLE; /snmp set vrf=$MGMT_TABLE"
492:         rest_add "start management VRF handoff" execute "{\"script\":\"$(json_str "$_script")\"}"
493:     fi
494:     _start=$(date +%s)
495:     until mgmt_vrf_ready; do
496:         [ $(( $(date +%s) - _start )) -lt "$BOOT_WAIT" ] \
497:             || mgmt_fail "VRF handoff did not complete; inspect RouterOS script errors through the serial console"
498:         sleep 1
499:     done
500:     log "management VRF $MGMT_TABLE: ether1, routing table and service bindings verified"
501: }
502: # The tagged objects already match the container's addressing (a restart with
503: # the same IP): leave them alone, re-applying would only drop live sessions.
504: mgmt_in_place() {
505:     _want=0
506:     rest_has "ip/vrf?name=$MGMT_TABLE&interfaces=ether1&comment=$MGMT_COMMENT&disabled=false" || return 1
507:     if [ -n "$M4" ]; then
508:         rest_has "ip/address?interface=ether1&address=$M4&comment=$MGMT_COMMENT" || return 1
509:         [ -z "$G4" ] || rest_has "ip/route?routing-table=$MGMT_TABLE&dst-address=0.0.0.0/0&gateway=$G4@$MGMT_TABLE" || return 1
510:         _want=$((_want + 1))
511:     fi
512:     if [ -n "$M6" ]; then
513:         rest_has "ipv6/address?interface=ether1&address=$M6&comment=$MGMT_COMMENT" || return 1
514:         [ -z "$G6" ] || rest_has "ipv6/route?routing-table=$MGMT_TABLE&dst-address=::/0&gateway=$G6@$MGMT_TABLE" || return 1
515:         _want=$((_want + 1))
516:     fi
517:     [ "$(rest_count "ip/address?comment=$MGMT_COMMENT")$(rest_count "ipv6/address?comment=$MGMT_COMMENT")" \
518:         = "$([ -n "$M4" ] && echo 1 || echo 0)$([ -n "$M6" ] && echo 1 || echo 0)" ] || return 1
519:     rest_has "ipv6/nd?interface=ether1&ra-lifetime=none" || return 1
520:     [ "$_want" -gt 0 ]
521: }
522: mgmt_setup() {
523:     mgmt_vrf
524:     if mgmt_in_place; then
525:         log "management on ether1 unchanged: ${M4:-no IPv4}${M6:+, $M6}"
526:         return 0
527:     fi
528:     for _m in ip/route ipv6/route ip/address ipv6/address; do rest_clear "$_m"; done
529:     _c="\"comment\":\"$MGMT_COMMENT\""
530:     if [ -n "$M4" ]; then
531:         rest_add "ether1 address $M4" ip/address/add "{\"address\":\"$M4\",\"interface\":\"ether1\",$_c}"
532:         [ -z "$G4" ] || rest_add "default via $G4 in VRF $MGMT_TABLE" ip/route/add \
533:             "{\"dst-address\":\"0.0.0.0/0\",\"gateway\":\"$G4@$MGMT_TABLE\",\"routing-table\":\"$MGMT_TABLE\",$_c}"
534:     fi
535:     if [ -n "$M6" ]; then
536:         rest_add "ether1 address $M6" ipv6/address/add \
537:             "{\"address\":\"$M6\",\"interface\":\"ether1\",\"advertise\":\"no\",$_c}"
538:         [ -z "$G6" ] || rest_add "IPv6 default via $G6 in VRF $MGMT_TABLE" ipv6/route/add \
539:             "{\"dst-address\":\"::/0\",\"gateway\":\"$G6@$MGMT_TABLE\",\"routing-table\":\"$MGMT_TABLE\",$_c}"
540:     fi
541:     _id="$(rest "$AUTH" "ip/dhcp-client?interface=ether1" | sed -n 's/.*"\.id":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -n1)"
542:     [ -z "$_id" ] || rest_add "disable the ether1 DHCP client" ip/dhcp-client/set \
543:         "{\"numbers\":\"$_id\",\"disabled\":\"yes\"}"
544:     # RouterOS's default ND entry (interface=all, ra-lifetime=30m) sends router
545:     # advertisements on ether1 too, and every host on the management network
546:     # with accept_ra would install the router as its IPv6 default route. An
547:     # ether1 entry with ra-lifetime=none keeps the RAs harmless and withdraws a
548:     # route a host already learned (a disabled entry does not override "all").
549:     # /ipv6/nd keeps no comment, so its entry is found by interface.
550:     _nd="$(rest "$AUTH" "ipv6/nd?interface=ether1" | sed -n 's/.*"\.id":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -n1)"
551:     if [ -n "$_nd" ]; then
552:         rest_add "ether1 router advertisements off" ipv6/nd/set \
553:             "{\"numbers\":\"$_nd\",\"ra-lifetime\":\"none\",\"disabled\":\"no\"}"
554:     else
555:         rest_add "ether1 router advertisements off" ipv6/nd/add \
556:             "{\"interface\":\"ether1\",\"ra-lifetime\":\"none\"}"
557:     fi
558:     # Prove they took (a transport flake answers an empty body, which is not
559:     # an error by the set-contract).
560:     if [ -n "$M4" ]; then
561:         rest_has "ip/address?interface=ether1&address=$M4" || mgmt_fail "$M4 not on ether1"
562:     fi
563:     mgmt_in_place || mgmt_fail "management addressing or routes not applied"
564:     log "management on ether1: ${M4:-no IPv4}${M6:+, $M6}, return path in VRF $MGMT_TABLE"
565: }
566: # Join the management network, then have the router reach its gateway from the
567: # management address: proves the return path both ways, and the ARP/ND request
568: # refreshes the gateway's neighbor entry when the IP was used by another MAC
569: # before (a redeployed lab hands out the same addresses).
570: mgmt_attach() {
571:     [ -e "$SYSNET/$MGMT_BR/brif/eth0" ] || brctl addif "$MGMT_BR" eth0
572:     ip link set eth0 up
573:     for _pair in "$G4 ${M4%/*}" "$G6 ${M6%/*}"; do
574:         # shellcheck disable=SC2086  # split "gateway source"; an empty half skips the pair
575:         set -- $_pair
576:         [ $# -eq 2 ] || continue
577:         _t0=$(date +%s)
578:         until case "$(rest "$AUTH" ping "{\"address\":\"$1\",\"src-address\":\"$2\",\"count\":\"2\",\"vrf\":\"$MGMT_TABLE\"}")" in
579:                 *'"received":"'[1-9]*) true ;; *) false ;; esac; do
580:             if [ $(( $(date +%s) - _t0 )) -ge 30 ]; then
581:                 log "gateway $1 does not answer from $2 after $(( $(date +%s) - _t0 ))s (continuing)"
582:                 break
583:             fi
584:             sleep 1
585:         done
586:     done
587: }
588: 
589: # Bootstrap + startup-config import happen ONCE per container lifetime. On a
590: # restart the CHR disk keeps its config and the marker (in the container rw
591: # layer) survives, so the bootstrap (which could wait forever if the config
592: # disabled `www` or changed the account, or reject duplicate `add` lines) is
593: # skipped. A fresh deploy recreates the container and the disk, so the marker
594: # and the config are both gone and the bootstrap runs.
595: if [ -f "$DONE_MARKER" ]; then
596:     log "already bootstrapped (restart): skipping config"
597:     mgmt_setup
598:     mgmt_attach
599:     ready
600:     wait "$QEMU_PID"
601:     exit 0
602: fi
603: 
604: # ---- credentials + identity -----------------------------------------------
605: # Every credential-establishing call is CHECKED: the ready marker never
606: # advertises credentials that do not work.
607: FACTORY="admin:"
608: rest "$FACTORY" system/resource >/dev/null 2>&1 || FACTORY="admin:$PASSWORD"
609: if [ "$USERNAME" = "admin" ]; then
610:     if [ -n "$PASSWORD" ]; then
611:         out="$(rest "$FACTORY" user/set \
612:             "{\"numbers\":\"admin\",\"password\":\"$(json_str "$PASSWORD")\"}")"
613:         is_err "$out" && bootstrap_fail "set admin password: ${out:-no response}"
614:     fi
615:     AUTH="admin:$PASSWORD"
616: else
617:     out="$(rest "$FACTORY" user/add \
618:         "{\"name\":\"$(json_str "$USERNAME")\",\"password\":\"$(json_str "$PASSWORD")\",\"group\":\"full\"}")"
619:     is_err "$out" && bootstrap_fail "create user $USERNAME: ${out:-no response}"
620:     AUTH="$USERNAME:$PASSWORD"
621:     # The factory `admin` still has a BLANK password and is reachable over the
622:     # forwarded services: disable it so the node keeps no unauthenticated
623:     # full-access account.
624:     out="$(rest "$AUTH" user/set "{\"numbers\":\"admin\",\"disabled\":\"yes\"}")"
625:     is_err "$out" && bootstrap_fail "disable factory admin: ${out:-no response}"
626:     if rest "admin:" system/resource >/dev/null 2>&1; then
627:         bootstrap_fail "factory admin still authenticates after disable"
628:     fi
629: fi
630: rest "$AUTH" system/resource >/dev/null 2>&1 \
631:     || bootstrap_fail "the requested credentials do not authenticate"
632: out="$(rest "$AUTH" system/identity/set "{\"name\":\"$(json_str "$HOSTNAME_ARG")\"}")"
633: is_err "$out" && bootstrap_fail "set identity: ${out:-no response}"
634: got="$(rest "$AUTH" system/identity)"
635: case "$got" in
636:     *"\"name\":\"$HOSTNAME_ARG\""*) : ;;
637:     *) bootstrap_fail "identity not applied: ${got:-no response}" ;;
638: esac
639: 
640: mgmt_setup
641: mgmt_attach
642: 
643: # ---- startup config -------------------------------------------------------
644: if [ -s "$STARTUP_CFG" ]; then
645:     bridge_ll
646:     # one-shot HTTP server on the bridge's link-local address; the router
647:     # fetches from it through ether1 (fetch takes a zoned link-local address
648:     # only as `address=`, not inside a URL)
649:     {
650:         printf 'HTTP/1.0 200 OK\r\nContent-Type: text/plain\r\nContent-Length: %s\r\n\r\n' \
651:             "$(wc -c < "$STARTUP_CFG")"
652:         cat "$STARTUP_CFG"
653:     } | timeout 90 nc -l -s "$LL%$MGMT_BR" -p "$FETCH_PORT" >/dev/null 2>&1 &
654:     sleep 1
655:     fetch="$(rest "$AUTH" tool/fetch \
656:         "{\"address\":\"$LL%ether1@$MGMT_TABLE\",\"port\":\"$FETCH_PORT\",\"src-path\":\"/config.auto.rsc\",\"mode\":\"http\",\"dst-path\":\"config.auto.rsc\"}")"
657:     case "$fetch" in
658:         *'"status":"finished"'*)
659:             # /import answers only when it finishes: a large config gets
660:             # CHR_BOOT_WAIT seconds.
661:             result="$(rest_raw "$AUTH" import '{"file-name":"config.auto.rsc"}' "$BOOT_WAIT")"
662:             case "$result" in
663:                 *'"ret":"true"'*)
664:                     log "startup config imported"
665:                     ;;
666:                 *)
667:                     # RouterOS imports line by line and stops at the first
668:                     # error: the lines before it ARE applied.
669:                     detail="$(printf '%s' "$result" | sed -n 's/.*"detail":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')"
670:                     log "startup config import FAILED: ${detail:-${result:-no response}}; lines before the failing one were applied, the rest were not"
671:                     wait "$QEMU_PID"
672:                     exit 0
673:                     ;;
674:             esac
675:             ;;
676:         *)
677:             log "startup config import FAILED: fetch did not finish: ${fetch:-no response}"
678:             wait "$QEMU_PID"
679:             exit 0
680:             ;;
681:     esac
682: fi
683: 
684: touch "$DONE_MARKER" 2>/dev/null || true
685: ready
686: wait "$QEMU_PID"

(End of file - total 686 lines)

    "output": "<path>/source/head/nodes/mikrotik_chr/chr-launch.sh</path>\n<type>file</type>\n<content>\n1: #!/bin/sh\n2: # chr-launch.sh: run the OFFICIAL mikrotik/chr image (MikroTik RouterOS Cloud\n3: # Hosted Router) as a containerlab node, image untouched.\n4: #\n5: # The image is MikroTik's own Docker Hub distribution (Alpine + qemu +\n6: # /diskimage/chr-<ver>.img + /start.sh). This script is bind-mounted into the\n7: # node and set as its entrypoint by the containerlab `mikrotik_chr` kind. It replaces\n8: # the image's /start.sh, which is not orchestration-ready (containerlab#3116):\n9: # it scans interfaces once before containerlab attaches the links, bridges the\n10: # management NIC so the container IP never reaches the router, and imports no\n11: # startup config.\n12: #\n13: # What it does (vrnetlab's mikrotik/routeros launch.py is the model, re-done\n14: # with the image's own busybox + qemu: no python, no ftp client, no tc):\n15: #   1. waits for the CLAB_INTFS data interfaces containerlab attaches (eth1..N)\n16: #   2. management, transparent: the container's eth0 is bridged with the VM's\n17: #      ether1 tap, and eth0's addresses and default gateways move into RouterOS\n18: #      ether1. The router IS the node's management address: every service and\n19: #      LLDP reach it directly, nothing is port-forwarded. The image ships only\n20: #      busybox (no tc), so this uses a bridge where vrnetlab uses tc-mirred\n21: #   3. data: one tap per container interface, bridged pairwise (ethN <-> tapN,\n22: #      LLDP forwarded). NIC order in the VM follows the eth index, so container\n23: #      ethN is always RouterOS ether(N+1), even with gaps\n24: #   4. after boot, over IPv6 link-local on the management bridge (no address is\n25: #      added to the management network): sets the credentials and the identity,\n26: #      configures ether1 with the management addresses and keeps their return\n27: #      path in its own VRF (`mgmt`, below), then fetches\n28: #      /ftpboot/config.auto.rsc (the containerlab startup-config, when present)\n29: #      from the launcher and `/import`s it\n30: #   5. prints the ready marker on the container log and waits on qemu\n31: #\n32: # Restart (docker restart, containerlab restart --node): RouterOS keys an\n33: # ethernet interface on its MAC. A NIC that comes back with a new MAC is a NEW\n34: # device (ether1 becomes ether3) and the DHCP client bound to ether1 never\n35: # binds. Docker re-rolls the container's eth0 MAC whenever the netns is\n36: # recreated, so the node id that seeds every NIC MAC and the data NIC count are\n37: # persisted in the container on the first boot and reused: the restarted qemu\n38: # carries the same NICs in the same order and RouterOS keeps ether1..N and\n39: # their config. The REST bootstrap is skipped on a restart; the management\n40: # step re-runs and re-applies the container's current addressing.\n41: #\n42: # Architectures: the image's own qemu (qemu-system-x86_64 on amd64,\n43: #   qemu-system-aarch64 + edk2 on arm64), KVM when /dev/kvm exists, else TCG.\n44: # Args (the kind's Cmd): --hostname H [--username U --password P]\n45: #   (unknown flags are ignored); credentials default to the USERNAME/PASSWORD env\n46: # Env (all optional, set under the node's `env:`); MEM, CPUS and DISK are the\n47: #   official image's own variables:\n48: #   MEM (qemu -m value, default 256 MiB + 8 MiB per data NIC and vCPU), CPUS (default 1),\n49: #   DISK (default 128M), CHR_INTF_WAIT (s, 60), CHR_BOOT_WAIT (s, 300)\n50: # Serial console: port 5000 inside the container\n51: #   (docker exec -it <node> nc 127.0.0.1 5000); the container itself has no\n52: #   address on the management network.\n53: # Ready: /.chr-launch-ready exists once RouterOS is ready (the kind's default\n54: #   healthcheck); it is removed at every start.\n55: # Log lines (docker logs clab-<lab>-<node>), all prefixed \"chr-launch:\":\n56: #   \"RouterOS ready\"                   login + startup config done\n57: #   \"startup config import FAILED: …\"  the router rejected the .rsc (RouterOS's\n58: #                                      own reason, with the line number)\n59: #   \"credential bootstrap FAILED: …\"   the user/password step failed\n60: #   \"management setup FAILED: …\"       the ether1 address / mgmt VRF step failed\n61: #\n62: # Copyright 2026 NetPilot Labs\n63: # Licensed under the BSD 3-Clause License.\n64: # SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause\n65: \n66: set -u\n67: \n68: # Credentials come from the USERNAME/PASSWORD env the kind sets (no quoting\n69: # limits on the password); --username/--password still override them.\n70: USERNAME=\"${USERNAME:-admin}\"\n71: PASSWORD=\"${PASSWORD-admin}\"\n72: HOSTNAME_ARG=\"\"\n73: while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do\n74:     case \"$1\" in\n75:         --username) USERNAME=\"$2\"; shift 2 ;;\n76:         --password) PASSWORD=\"$2\"; shift 2 ;;\n77:         --hostname) HOSTNAME_ARG=\"$2\"; shift 2 ;;\n78:         --connection-mode) shift 2 ;;\n79:         --trace) shift ;;\n80:         *) shift ;;\n81:     esac\n82: done\n83: [ -n \"$HOSTNAME_ARG\" ] || HOSTNAME_ARG=\"$(hostname)\"\n84: \n85: CPUS=\"${CPUS:-1}\"\n86: DISK=\"${DISK:-128M}\"\n87: INTF_WAIT=\"${CHR_INTF_WAIT:-60}\"\n88: BOOT_WAIT=\"${CHR_BOOT_WAIT:-300}\"\n89: INTFS=\"${CLAB_INTFS:-0}\"\n90: STARTUP_CFG=/ftpboot/config.auto.rsc\n91: # Per-container state in the rw layer: survives every restart, gone with the\n92: # container (destroy, redeploy --cleanup).\n93: DONE_MARKER=/.chr-launch-bootstrapped\n94: READY_FILE=/.chr-launch-ready\n95: ID_FILE=/.chr-launch-node-id\n96: NICS_FILE=/.chr-launch-nics\n97: MGMT_TABLE=mgmt\n98: # every management object the launcher creates carries this comment, so each\n99: # boot can find and re-apply them, and SaveConfig can leave them out\n100: MGMT_COMMENT=clab-mgmt\n101: MGMT_BR=br0\n102: # eth0's addressing as last seen: a launcher re-run in the same network\n103: # namespace finds eth0 already bridged and bare\n104: MGMT_FILE=/.chr-launch-mgmt\n105: SYSNET=/sys/class/net\n106: \n107: log() { echo \"chr-launch: $*\"; }\n108: rm -f \"$READY_FILE\"\n109: \n110: FETCH_PORT=8080\n111: \n112: # ---- disk -----------------------------------------------------------------\n113: IMG=\"\"\n114: for f in /diskimage/*.img; do [ -f \"$f\" ] && IMG=\"$f\" && break; done\n115: if [ -z \"$IMG\" ]; then\n116:     log \"no /diskimage/*.img in this image: not a RouterOS CHR image\"\n117:     exit 1\n118: fi\n119: # Only GROW the disk to the floor: an image already larger keeps its tail.\n120: disk_bytes() {\n121:     case \"$1\" in\n122:         *G|*g) echo $(( ${1%[Gg]} * 1024 * 1024 * 1024 )) ;;\n123:         *M|*m) echo $(( ${1%[Mm]} * 1024 * 1024 )) ;;\n124:         *K|*k) echo $(( ${1%[Kk]} * 1024 )) ;;\n125:         *) echo \"$1\" ;;\n126:     esac\n127: }\n128: want_bytes=\"$(disk_bytes \"$DISK\")\"\n129: cur_bytes=\"$(stat -c %s \"$IMG\" 2>/dev/null || wc -c < \"$IMG\")\"\n130: if [ \"$cur_bytes\" -lt \"$want_bytes\" ] 2>/dev/null; then\n131:     truncate -s \"$DISK\" \"$IMG\"\n132: fi\n133: \n134: # ---- wait for containerlab's data interfaces ------------------------------\n135: # shellcheck disable=SC2012  # interface names are ethN, ls is safe here\n136: count_intfs() { ls -d \"$SYSNET\"/eth[1-9]* 2>/dev/null | wc -l; }\n137: waited=0\n138: while [ \"$(count_intfs)\" -lt \"$INTFS\" ] && [ \"$waited\" -lt \"$INTF_WAIT\" ]; do\n139:     sleep 1\n140:     waited=$((waited + 1))\n141: done\n142: log \"interfaces: $(count_intfs) of $INTFS expected after ${waited}s\"\n143: \n144: # ---- qemu command line ----------------------------------------------------\n145: # The image's own qemu and firmware, as its /start.sh selects them.\n146: case \"$(uname -m)\" in\n147:     aarch64|arm64)\n148:         QEMU=\"qemu-system-aarch64 -M virt -pflash /usr/share/qemu/edk2-aarch64-code.fd\"\n149:         TCG_CPU=\"-cpu cortex-a57\" ;;\n150:     *)\n151:         QEMU=\"qemu-system-x86_64\"\n152:         TCG_CPU=\"\" ;;\n153: esac\n154: if [ -e /dev/kvm ]; then\n155:     ACCEL=\"-cpu host -accel kvm\"\n156: else\n157:     ACCEL=\"$TCG_CPU -accel tcg,split-wx=on\"\n158:     log \"no /dev/kvm: running under TCG emulation (slow boot)\"\n159: fi\n160: \n161: # MACs: unique per node AND per NIC. The container's eth0 MAC is unique per\n162: # node, so its LAST TWO octets identify the node; the NIC's last byte is the\n163: # interface index (00 = mgmt, 01 = ether2, …). Two nodes sharing a NIC MAC on\n164: # a link drop each other's frames as their own. The id is read on the FIRST\n165: # boot only and persisted (see Restart in the header).\n166: node_id=\"$(cat \"$ID_FILE\" 2>/dev/null)\"\n167: case \"$node_id\" in\n168:     [0-9a-f][0-9a-f]:[0-9a-f][0-9a-f]) ;;\n169:     *)\n170:         e=\"$(cat \"$SYSNET/eth0/address\" 2>/dev/null)\"\n171:         if [ -n \"$e\" ]; then\n172:             o2=\"${e##*:}\"; rest_mac=\"${e%:*}\"; o1=\"${rest_mac##*:}\"\n173:             node_id=\"$o1:$o2\"\n174:         else\n175:             node_id=\"$(hexdump -n2 -e '2/1 \"%02x:\"' /dev/urandom | sed 's/:$//')\"\n176:         fi\n177:         printf '%s\\n' \"$node_id\" > \"$ID_FILE\" 2>/dev/null \\\n178:             || log \"node id $node_id not persisted: a restart will renumber the NICs\"\n179:         ;;\n180: esac\n181: NET=\"-netdev tap,id=mgmt,ifname=tap0,script=no,downscript=no -device virtio-net,netdev=mgmt,mac=52:54:00:$node_id:00\"\n182: \n183: # ---- management: eth0 + tap0 on one bridge, eth0's addressing to the VM ----\n184: ip_global() { # ip_global <4|6> <dev>: the first global address/prefix\n185:     ip -\"$1\" addr show dev \"$2\" 2>/dev/null \\\n186:         | sed -n '/scope global/s/^ *inet6\\{0,1\\} \\([^ ]*\\) .*/\\1/p' | head -n1\n187: }\n188: ip_gw() { # ip_gw <4|6>: the default gateway\n189:     ip -\"$1\" route show default 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^default via \\([^ ]*\\) .*/\\1/p' | head -n1\n190: }\n191: M4=\"$(ip_global 4 eth0)\"; M6=\"$(ip_global 6 eth0)\"\n192: G4=\"$(ip_gw 4)\"; G6=\"$(ip_gw 6)\"\n193: if [ -n \"$M4$M6\" ]; then\n194:     printf 'M4=%s\\nM6=%s\\nG4=%s\\nG6=%s\\n' \"$M4\" \"$M6\" \"$G4\" \"$G6\" > \"$MGMT_FILE\" 2>/dev/null || true\n195: elif [ -f \"$MGMT_FILE\" ]; then\n196:     # shellcheck disable=SC1090  # written by this script, four plain assignments\n197:     . \"$MGMT_FILE\"\n198: fi\n199: log \"management: ${M4:-no IPv4}${M6:+, $M6} via ${G4:-no gateway}${G6:+, $G6}\"\n200: \n201: tunctl -t tap0 >/dev/null 2>&1 || ip tuntap add dev tap0 mode tap\n202: if [ ! -e \"$SYSNET/$MGMT_BR\" ]; then\n203:     _mtu=\"$(cat \"$SYSNET/eth0/mtu\" 2>/dev/null || echo 1500)\"\n204:     ip addr flush dev eth0\n205:     # The launcher's side of the bootstrap channel: IPv6 link-local on the\n206:     # bridge only. eth0 and tap0 are plain bridge ports.\n207:     sysctl -qw net.ipv6.conf.default.disable_ipv6=0 net.ipv6.conf.default.accept_ra=0 2>/dev/null\n208:     brctl addbr \"$MGMT_BR\"\n209:     brctl setfd \"$MGMT_BR\" 0 2>/dev/null\n210:     echo 16384 > \"$SYSNET/$MGMT_BR/bridge/group_fwd_mask\" 2>/dev/null\n211:     ip link set \"$MGMT_BR\" address \"52:54:01:$node_id:00\"\n212:     ip link set tap0 mtu \"$_mtu\"\n213:     ip link set \"$MGMT_BR\" mtu \"$_mtu\"\n214:     # eth0 joins the bridge only once ether1 is configured (mgmt_attach): until\n215:     # then nothing the router sends (its boot-time router advertisements, CHR's\n216:     # DHCP discovers) reaches the management network.\n217:     brctl addif \"$MGMT_BR\" tap0\n218:     sysctl -qw net.ipv6.conf.eth0.disable_ipv6=1 net.ipv6.conf.tap0.disable_ipv6=1 \\\n219:         \"net.ipv6.conf.$MGMT_BR.disable_ipv6=0\" \"net.ipv6.conf.$MGMT_BR.accept_ra=0\" \\\n220:         \"net.ipv6.conf.$MGMT_BR.router_solicitations=0\" 2>/dev/null\n221: fi\n222: ip link set tap0 up\n223: ip link set \"$MGMT_BR\" up\n224: # RouterOS's ether1 link-local address, from the MAC this script gives it\n225: VM_LL=\"fe80::5054:ff:fe${node_id%%:*}:${node_id##*:}00\"\n226: VM_EP=\"$VM_LL%$MGMT_BR\"\n227: # The bridge's own link-local address (the startup-config fetch source). Read\n228: # once qemu runs: until then tap0, the bridge's only port, has no carrier and\n229: # the address stays tentative.\n230: LL=\"\"\n231: bridge_ll() {\n232:     _w=0\n233:     while [ -z \"$LL\" ] && [ \"$_w\" -lt 20 ]; do\n234:         LL=\"$(ip -6 addr show dev \"$MGMT_BR\" 2>/dev/null | grep -v tentative \\\n235:             | sed -n 's/^ *inet6 \\(fe80::[^/]*\\)\\/64 .*/\\1/p' | head -n1)\"\n236:         [ -n \"$LL\" ] || { sleep 1; _w=$((_w + 1)); }\n237:     done\n238:     [ -n \"$LL\" ] || log \"no IPv6 link-local on $MGMT_BR\"\n239: }\n240: \n241: # NIC order = PCI order = the order of the -device args below. Walk\n242: # eth1..ethMAX so a gap (links on ether2 and ether5 only) keeps RouterOS\n243: # numbering aligned: a missing ethN still gets a tap, just no bridge. The count\n244: # never shrinks across restarts: a `docker restart` recreates the netns and\n245: # every lab veth of the node is gone, and a NIC absent for one boot loses the\n246: # config bound to it. The tap keeps ether(N+1) a real interface, its link comes\n247: # back when containerlab restores the veth or the lab is redeployed.\n248: max=0\n249: for d in \"$SYSNET\"/eth[1-9]*; do\n250:     [ -e \"$d\" ] || continue\n251:     n=\"${d##*/eth}\"\n252:     [ \"$n\" -gt \"$max\" ] && max=\"$n\"\n253: done\n254: prev=\"$(cat \"$NICS_FILE\" 2>/dev/null)\"\n255: case \"$prev\" in *[!0-9]*|\"\") prev=0 ;; esac\n256: [ \"$prev\" -gt \"$max\" ] && max=\"$prev\"\n257: # The wait above can end short of CLAB_INTFS on a large lab (links attach after\n258: # every container started): the NIC set still spans the expected count, and\n259: # the watcher bridges the late veths.\n260: case \"$INTFS\" in *[!0-9]*|\"\") INTFS=0 ;; esac\n261: [ \"$INTFS\" -gt \"$max\" ] && max=\"$INTFS\"\n262: [ \"$max\" -gt \"$prev\" ] && { printf '%s\\n' \"$max\" > \"$NICS_FILE\" 2>/dev/null || true; }\n263: \n264: # RouterOS v7 memory ≈ 256 + 8·CPUS·(ifaces) MiB (MikroTik CHR system\n265: # requirements). Scale by the HIGHEST generated NIC, not CLAB_INTFS: a sparse\n266: # link on ether64 means CLAB_INTFS=1 yet 63 data NICs are created below.\n267: if [ -z \"${MEM:-}\" ]; then\n268:     MEM=$((256 + 8 * CPUS * max))\n269: fi\n270: \n271: bridge_eth() { # bridge_eth <i>: container ethI joins brI beside tapI (brI made once)\n272:     _mtu=\"$(cat \"$SYSNET/eth$1/mtu\" 2>/dev/null || echo 1500)\"\n273:     if [ ! -e \"$SYSNET/br$1\" ]; then\n274:         brctl addbr \"br$1\"\n275:         ip link set \"br$1\" mtu \"$_mtu\"\n276:         ip link set \"tap$1\" mtu \"$_mtu\"\n277:         # forward LLDP (01:80:c2:00:00:0e, bit 14); STP/LACP cannot cross a bridge\n278:         echo 16384 > \"$SYSNET/br$1/bridge/group_fwd_mask\" 2>/dev/null\n279:         brctl addif \"br$1\" \"tap$1\"\n280:     fi\n281:     brctl addif \"br$1\" \"eth$1\"\n282:     ip link set \"eth$1\" up\n283:     ip link set \"br$1\" up\n284: }\n285: # A veth that lands or returns while qemu runs (containerlab restores a link\n286: # right after a restart --node, a large lab attaches late, a peer node's\n287: # redeploy recreates the pair) joins its bridge as it appears, so the RouterOS\n288: # interface behind tapN gets its link back without a restart here.\n289: watch_links() {\n290:     _warned=\"\"\n291:     while kill -0 \"$QEMU_PID\" 2>/dev/null; do\n292:         i=1\n293:         while [ \"$i\" -le \"$max\" ]; do\n294:             if [ -e \"$SYSNET/eth$i\" ] && [ ! -e \"$SYSNET/br$i/brif/eth$i\" ]; then\n295:                 bridge_eth \"$i\" && log \"link eth$i attached: bridged to tap$i\"\n296:             fi\n297:             i=$((i + 1))\n298:         done\n299:         for d in \"$SYSNET\"/eth[1-9]*; do\n300:             [ -e \"$d\" ] || continue\n301:             n=\"${d##*/eth}\"\n302:             [ \"$n\" -gt \"$max\" ] || continue\n303:             case \" $_warned \" in *\" $n \"*) continue ;; esac\n304:             _warned=\"$_warned $n\"\n305:             log \"link eth$n attached after qemu started with $max data NICs: no RouterOS interface for it until the node is restarted\"\n306:         done\n307:         sleep 2\n308:     done\n309: }\n310: \n311: i=1\n312: while [ \"$i\" -le \"$max\" ]; do\n313:     tap=\"tap$i\"\n314:     tunctl -t \"$tap\" >/dev/null 2>&1 || ip tuntap add dev \"$tap\" mode tap\n315:     [ -e \"$SYSNET/eth$i\" ] && bridge_eth \"$i\"\n316:     ip link set \"$tap\" up\n317:     mac=\"$(printf '52:54:00:%s:%02x' \"$node_id\" \"$((i & 255))\")\"\n318:     NET=\"$NET -netdev tap,id=d$i,ifname=$tap,script=no,downscript=no -device virtio-net,netdev=d$i,mac=$mac\"\n319:     i=$((i + 1))\n320: done\n321: \n322: # shellcheck disable=SC2086\n323: $QEMU $ACCEL -display none -monitor none \\\n324:     -m \"$MEM\" -smp \"cpus=$CPUS\" \\\n325:     -drive \"file=$IMG,format=raw\" \\\n326:     -serial telnet:0.0.0.0:5000,server,nowait \\\n327:     $NET &\n328: QEMU_PID=$!\n329: trap 'kill \"$QEMU_PID\" 2>/dev/null;
